project_and_compatibility.implementation_language: Playwright and Playwright Test are primarily implemented in TypeScript. Tests can be authored in TypeScript or JavaScript and run on Node.js. The evaluated npm package is @playwright/test.
project_and_compatibility.node_and_typescript_compatibility: Node.js 24 is officially supported: the current system requirements list the latest Node.js 22.x, 24.x, or 26.x, @playwright/test 1.62.1 declares node >=20, and its npm metadata records publication with Node 24.18.0. This repository selects Node 24.12 in .nvmrc and TypeScript 6.0.3 with ESNext modules and bundler resolution. Playwright transpiles TypeScript tests without requiring the application's compiler, but a repository-local install and execution against TypeScript 6.0.3 was not performed, so complete TypeScript 6 configuration compatibility is [uncertain].
project_and_compatibility.operating_system_support: Officially supported Linux targets include Debian 12/13 and Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 on x86-64 and arm64. These cover local supported Linux installations and GitHub-hosted Ubuntu x86-64 runners. Official Ubuntu-based Docker images are available. Firefox and WebKit browser builds require glibc, so Alpine and other musl distributions are not supported for those engines.
project_and_compatibility.license_and_governance: Apache License 2.0. The project is owned and commercially stewarded by Microsoft in the microsoft/playwright repository, developed in public, and accepts community contributions under repository contribution rules. The permissive license allows use, modification, and redistribution in this repository subject to Apache-2.0 notice and patent terms; no paid license is required.
project_and_compatibility.installation_model: Add @playwright/test as a development dependency, normally with npm install -D @playwright/test, then install version-matched browsers with npx playwright install or a selected engine. On Linux CI, npx playwright install --with-deps installs browser binaries and operating-system libraries. Versioned Microsoft Container Registry images such as mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.0-noble include browsers and system dependencies but not the project's test package. Browser binaries are large external artifacts stored in Playwright's cache unless a custom PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is used.
project_and_compatibility.candidate_scope_and_layer: Complete E2E framework: integrated test runner, assertions, fixtures, isolation, parallel workers, browser management, API requests, reports, retries, traces, screenshots, video, code generation, and debugging tools.
project_and_compatibility.authoring_and_async_model: Native TypeScript/JavaScript async and await with test, expect, fixtures, hooks, projects, and configuration APIs. Browser operations return promises; there is no hidden command queue or required Gherkin/keyword DSL. Web-first locator assertions retry asynchronously and must be awaited.
project_and_compatibility.build_pipeline_coupling: Black-box tests can target either the production image built by Parcel and served with the Gin backend or the Parcel development server. Playwright does not require Vite, application source transformation, browser instrumentation, or replacement of Parcel. In production, this repository serves the frontend and /api from one Gin origin on port 80. In development, Parcel serves port 8000 and .proxyrc.js proxies /api to Gin on port 8080; baseURL can point to either arrangement.
project_and_compatibility.testability_instrumentation_required: No production instrumentation, special route, injected script, relaxed content-security policy, or build hook is required. Existing semantic roles, labels, visible text, IDs, and attributes can be used. Adding stable data-testid attributes is optional where the current dynamic templates do not expose a unique user-facing locator. Test-only API fixture/reset endpoints would be optional custom application work, not a Playwright requirement; database setup can instead use existing APIs or direct fixture code outside production paths.

browser_and_runtime_coverage.browser_engines: Managed Chromium, patched Firefox, and patched WebKit are first-class projects. Chromium mode can also run installed Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge channels, including stable, beta, dev, and canary where available; branded browsers are not installed by default. Playwright does not drive stock Firefox or Safari because its Firefox and WebKit support relies on patches. Electron support exists but is not relevant to this web application.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.browser_protocol: Normal operation uses Playwright's own high-fidelity client/server protocol and patched browser integrations rather than W3C WebDriver or WebDriver BiDi. Chromium-only CDP sessions and connectOverCDP are available, but official documentation describes CDP attachment as lower fidelity than the Playwright protocol. This provides deep control and consistent APIs at the cost of protocol and managed-browser lock-in.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.headless_and_headed_modes: Headless execution is the default and fits CI. Headed mode is supported locally with headless: false or --headed; Linux CI can use Xvfb, which is present in official images. Debug mode launches headed browsers and the Inspector.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.browser_version_management: Each Playwright release is paired with tested browser revisions downloaded by npx playwright install. Updating @playwright/test generally requires reinstalling matching browsers. Teams can install only selected engines, set the browser cache path, use installed Chrome/Edge channels, or pin an official image tag. Arbitrary executablePath use is explicitly unsupported-risky. Linux system dependencies require install --with-deps or a matching image.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.parallel_browser_support: Configuration projects define browser, device, and environment matrices. Projects run the same tests across selected engines; --project selects subsets. Worker count controls local parallelism, --shard distributes tests across jobs, and blob reports can be merged. Database-sensitive suites can use one worker or serial groups while independent browser-only tests retain parallel execution.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.mobile_emulation: Built-in device descriptors configure viewport, screen, user agent, touch, device scale factor, mobile mode, and browser context. Pixel and iPhone-like projects are supported for responsive checks. This is emulation in desktop browser engines, not execution on physical Android or iOS devices.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.real_browser_fidelity: Chromium projects can use managed builds or installed Chrome/Edge channels. Firefox is a patched build near recent Firefox Stable, not branded Firefox. WebKit is built from upstream WebKit and is not Apple Safari; Safari packaging, OS integration, codecs, and release timing differ. Official guidance says macOS WebKit is closer to Safari for platform-sensitive features such as media, but true Safari coverage requires a separate Safari-capable system/tool.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.environment_determinism_controls: Per-project or per-test controls include viewport, screen, device scale, user agent, touch/mobile mode, locale, timezone, geolocation, permissions, color scheme, contrast, forced colors, and reduced motion. Clock controls Date, timers, animation frames, performance, and event timestamps. Screenshot assertions disable animations by default and can mask or style volatile areas. Playwright does not provide a general seeded replacement for Math.random or backend randomness; tests must inject or control those separately.

application_fit.dynamic_dom_synchronization: Strong fit for HTMX swaps and lazy Handlebars rendering. Locators resolve an up-to-date DOM element before each action, retry if elements detach during actionability checks, and web-first assertions poll until expected state. This directly addresses this repository's hx-get, hx-trigger, after-settle, and template replacement patterns. Tests should assert a meaningful post-swap state or await a specific response rather than use networkidle or fixed sleeps.
application_fit.routing_support: Playwright can navigate directly to deep links, assert URLs, wait for URL changes, use goBack/goForward, and observe history-driven DOM changes. Gin's fallback serves root HTML for non-API GET routes, which supports direct Navigo deep links, while the frontend uses Navigo strategy ALL. Route tests should use page.waitForURL or URL assertions when one action can trigger multiple history changes. Playwright disables BFCache by default for deterministic navigation; explicitly enabling BFCache is unsupported for reliable lifecycle tracking.
application_fit.locator_model: Role, label, placeholder, text, alt text, title, CSS, and configurable test-ID locators are available. Locators are strict for single-element actions and fail on ambiguous matches, which surfaces template ambiguity. They reacquire nodes after HTMX replacement. Prefer roles/labels/text, with existing stable IDs or optional test IDs for dynamic rows where accessible identity is insufficient.
application_fit.form_interaction: fill, clear, press, pressSequentially, focus, blur, check, selectOption, keyboard, mouse, and dispatchEvent cover realistic form flows. Actions perform visibility, stability, event-receivability, enabled, and editable checks as applicable, and native validation can be asserted through DOM state and messages. This can exercise the repository's input masks, hx-validate, blur/focus behavior, hidden values, and dynamically added allocation/history rows without bypassing browser behavior.
application_fit.canvas_and_download_support: Chart.js canvas can be validated through application-visible legends/labels and source data, page.evaluate inspection of Chart state or canvas pixels, targeted screenshots, and visual comparisons. Trace canvas rendering is not fully reliable and current release notes say canvas trace display is disabled by default, so traces alone should not prove chart correctness. Download events expose suggested filenames, streams, paths, failure state, and saveAs; payload contents can be parsed and asserted. No current browser-side download implementation was found in the inspected frontend, so a future download scenario needs its concrete format defined.
application_fit.network_and_api_access: APIRequestContext supports REST fixture seeding and postcondition checks. Browser request/response events, waitForResponse, page/context routing, fulfill/abort/continue/fetch, HAR recording/replay, and WebSocket inspection are available. Yahoo Finance calls can be replaced at the browser network layer if browser-originated, or through a mock service/configured backend fixture if Gin performs them server-side. Existing Go integration-test mock patterns can remain separate.
application_fit.same_origin_support: Direct support with no CORS change. Production can be tested through the consolidated Gin origin where static files and /api share host and port. Development can target Parcel at port 8000, whose proxy forwards /api to localhost:8080. A baseURL per project selects either topology.
application_fit.test_isolation: Every test receives a fresh BrowserContext equivalent to a new browser profile, isolating cookies, local storage, IndexedDB, permissions, and pages. API request contexts can also have isolated cookie stores. Database state is external to browser isolation; use unique IDs per worker, API/direct-database cleanup fixtures, a disposable PostgreSQL instance, or workers: 1 for shared mutable fixtures. Fixture teardown should restore state regardless of test outcome.
application_fit.external_server_model: Tests can run against any independently started application by setting baseURL from configuration or environment. webServer is optional, so local port 80 production Compose, Parcel port 8000, a CI service URL, or an externally managed environment can use the same black-box tests.
application_fit.application_lifecycle: webServer can launch one or multiple commands, poll a URL for readiness, apply startup timeouts, reuse a local server, and terminate its process group. Project dependencies or setup/teardown fixtures can run builds, Docker Compose, migrations, fixture setup, and cleanup with report/trace visibility. For this repository, a small custom wrapper is still needed because build.sh, start.sh, Flyway completion, PostgreSQL disposal, and destroy.sh are multi-service concerns; use explicit health/readiness checks and gracefulShutdown SIGTERM for Docker-related commands.
application_fit.visual_regression_workflow: Core screenshot baselines are generated on first run, committed, reviewed, and updated with --update-snapshots. Per-project/platform paths separate browser baselines. Assertions wait for consecutive stable screenshots and support masks, custom styles, disabled animations, threshold, maxDiffPixels, maxDiffPixelRatio, CSS/device scaling, and volatile-region suppression. Fonts, OS, browser versions, data, viewport, time, and Chart.js animation must be pinned. Canvas is suitable for targeted visual checks only after deterministic chart data and animation completion; semantic/data assertions should remain primary.
application_fit.accessibility_audit_integration: Official guidance integrates the open-source @axe-core/playwright package through reusable fixtures and test attachments. Core assertions cover accessible roles, names, descriptions, and ARIA YAML snapshots. This provides open-source reporting through standard attachments/JSON/JUnit/HTML, but automated axe checks detect only a subset of accessibility issues and must be complemented by manual assessment.

reliability.waiting_model: Actions auto-wait for strict single-element resolution and applicable visibility, stability, receives-events, enabled, editable, and attachment conditions. Locator assertions retry for up to their expectation timeout. Navigation and URL waits, event waits, request/response waits, locator waits, and expect.poll/toPass support explicit domain synchronization. Fixed waitForTimeout sleeps and blanket networkidle waits should be avoided for HTMX; assert the desired DOM or response instead.
reliability.flake_controls: Independent test, assertion, action, navigation, fixture, and global timeout scopes are configurable. Retries can be CI-only; v1.62 adds immediate or isolated retry strategy. Failed workers and browsers are discarded before subsequent work. --repeat-each, --last-failed, --workers=1, serial groups, trace retention modes, and failOnFlakyTests support reproduction and policy enforcement. Retries should expose rather than hide persistent shared-database defects.
reliability.isolation_model: Fresh BrowserContext and page fixtures are created per test, while worker processes isolate JavaScript globals and each worker launches a browser. A worker is replaced after failure. Serial groups and beforeAll-created shared pages are available for genuinely dependent scenarios, but the official recommendation is isolated tests. PostgreSQL must be isolated or reset separately because it sits outside the browser context.
reliability.resource_usage: Each worker is an OS process with its own browser, so CPU and memory increase with worker and browser-project count. Three managed engines plus Linux dependencies consume substantial download/cache and artifact disk space; video and trace retention can add significant storage. Installing only Chromium and limiting CI workers reduces cost. Repository-specific memory, disk, install-size, and duration measurements were not run, so quantitative resource usage is [uncertain].
reliability.parallelism_controls: Test files run in parallel by default while tests within a file run in declaration order. workers accepts an integer or CPU percentage; fullyParallel controls intra-file parallelism, serial mode protects dependent groups, project dependencies order setup, and shards distribute work across jobs. For the current shared PostgreSQL topology, start with workers: 1 for state-mutating E2E tests or allocate a unique database/schema and test-data namespace from testInfo.parallelIndex before increasing workers.
reliability.flake_observability: Reports classify passed-on-first-attempt, flaky-passed-on-retry, and failed tests; failOnFlakyTests can fail CI. retry and repeatEach expose recurrence, and JSON/JUnit/blob/custom reporters can export retry status for local trend processing. Traces can be retained from the first failed attempt or retries. There is no built-in long-term quarantine registry or historical dashboard in the open-source runner; quarantine tags and trend storage require repository conventions, a custom reporter, or an optional external service.

diagnostics_and_developer_experience.failure_artifacts: Configurable screenshots, videos, execution traces, attachments, HTML reports, and HAR files are available with on, failure-only, first-failure, or retry retention modes. Trace Viewer includes actions, before/after DOM snapshots, source, actionability logs, errors, console, and network request/response details. Browser console and page errors can also be attached through event listeners. Backend and Docker logs are not captured automatically.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.debugging_tools: Inspector supports pause, play, step, locator editing/picking, and actionability logs. UI Mode provides watch mode and time-travel-like exploration over trace snapshots, source, console, and network. Headed mode, slowMo, page.pause, browser DevTools, Node debuggers, and the official VS Code extension support interactive and breakpoint debugging.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.test_generation: Official codegen records clicks and fills, creates assertions, and generates role/text/test-id oriented locators through the Inspector or VS Code. Generated code is a starting point; dynamic HTMX waits, domain fixture setup, cleanup, and reusable page abstractions still require review and maintenance.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.reporters: Built-in list, line, dot, HTML, blob, JSON, JUnit, GitHub, and null reporters can be combined. Blob output supports shard merging; GitHub output creates annotations; custom reporters implement the reporter API. HTML reports link errors, steps, traces, and attachments.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.documentation_quality: High. Official versioned documentation covers installation, concepts, complete API references, examples, CI providers, Docker, migration-relevant release notes, debugging, authentication, accessibility, visual testing, network mocking, and common best practices. Fast release cadence means configuration should be checked against the pinned version rather than copied from next documentation.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.local_workflow: CLI filters support a file, line, title grep, tag, project/browser, last failures, headed mode, one worker, repeats, and debug mode. UI Mode runs or watches individual tests and groups interactively. The VS Code extension discovers, runs, debugs, and generates tests. npx playwright show-report and show-trace inspect prior artifacts without a hosted service.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.failure_log_correlation: Playwright timestamps and correlates browser actions, console entries, network traffic, assertions, and attachments inside the trace/report. Event listeners can attach failed-response and browser-error logs to testInfo. Gin, PostgreSQL, Flyway, and Docker Compose logs require custom setup/teardown or GitHub Actions steps that collect and attach/upload service logs, preferably with UTC timestamps and the run/test identifier. There is no automatic cross-process correlation.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.artifact_data_exposure: High sensitivity must be assumed. Official CI guidance warns that traces, reports, console logs, and screenshots can expose credentials, access tokens, test data, and source. HAR files may include headers, cookies, bodies, and portfolio records; storageState can contain impersonation-capable cookies, local storage, IndexedDB, and passkey private keys. Use synthetic data, omit/filter HAR content, sanitize custom attachments/logs, never commit auth state, restrict artifact access and retention, and encrypt external sharing. Trace Viewer itself processes traces locally in the browser and does not transmit them.

github_actions_fit.official_ci_support: Official GitHub Actions guidance uses actions/setup-node, npm ci, npx playwright install --with-deps, npx playwright test, and actions/upload-artifact. Versioned Ubuntu Docker images are maintained. No framework-specific GitHub Action is necessary. This repository currently has Go test/lint workflows only, so a Node 24 E2E job must be added.
github_actions_fit.browser_caching: Official documentation does not recommend caching Playwright browser binaries because restoring the cache is often comparable to downloading them and Linux system packages are not cacheable. npm dependencies can use setup-node's npm cache. Pin @playwright/test and install matching browsers, or pin the official Docker image; install only required engines to reduce time.
github_actions_fit.artifact_integration: Low effort: configure HTML plus blob/JSON/JUnit/GitHub reporters and upload playwright-report and selected test-results with actions/upload-artifact under if: !cancelled() or always() according to policy. Traces, screenshots, videos, and custom backend logs are ordinary files/attachments. Apply restricted access and short retention because artifacts may contain sensitive portfolio data.
github_actions_fit.sharding_and_matrix_support: Native --shard=i/n works with a GitHub matrix. Each shard can emit a blob report, and a dependent job can download and merge blobs into one HTML report. Browser projects can run inside one job or as a browser matrix. Retries occur within a shard; changing shard count or fullyParallel affects distribution. Database-mutating shards require independent databases/schemas or must remain unsharded.
github_actions_fit.container_compatibility: Can run directly on ubuntu-latest with install --with-deps or in a version-matched mcr.microsoft.com/playwright image. GitHub-hosted runners can also start this repository's Docker Compose services. If Playwright itself runs in a container, host/container networking must expose the application using a reachable hostname such as a host-gateway mapping; localhost refers to the test container. Official Docker guidance recommends --init and --ipc=host for Chromium stability.
github_actions_fit.failure_cleanup: Browser contexts, pages, worker fixtures, and webServer processes have runner-managed teardown; explicit context close ensures video/HAR flushing. Project teardown and global teardown can clean test data and services, and webServer can send SIGTERM before SIGKILL. Docker Compose, PostgreSQL volumes, and generated files remain repository responsibilities: GitHub Actions should run docker compose logs and docker compose down -v in an if: always() cleanup step, with unique project/volume names, because cancellation can bypass ordinary test teardown.

cost_and_risk.open_source_completeness: All required local and GitHub Actions capabilities evaluated here are available in the Apache-2.0 @playwright/test package and managed open-source browser builds: runner, browsers, fixtures, assertions, parallelism, sharding, API/network controls, screenshots, visual comparison, video, traces, HTML/JSON/JUnit/blob/GitHub reports, Inspector, UI Mode, and codegen. No paid service is required.
cost_and_risk.optional_cloud_dependency: None for execution, reports, trace viewing, visual baselines, or sharding. Third-party hosted dashboards, browser grids, and visual-testing services are optional. Equivalent core workflows can use local HTML/trace tools, committed baselines, GitHub artifacts, JSON/JUnit output, and repository-owned history processing, though open-source core does not provide a long-term hosted analytics dashboard.
cost_and_risk.migration_cost: Moderate framework lock-in. Tests use Playwright-specific locators, fixtures, expect matchers, projects, routing APIs, traces, and browser protocol; these would require rewriting for WebDriver/Cypress. Risk is reduced by standard TypeScript, async/await, accessible locator concepts, HTTP APIs, and black-box application boundaries. Keep domain fixture helpers and test data independent from page APIs where practical.
cost_and_risk.security_and_supply_chain: The package is Apache-2.0 and owned by Microsoft. @playwright/test 1.62.1 has a small direct npm surface, pinning playwright 1.62.1; npm metadata exposes integrity hashes, registry signatures, a SLSA provenance attestation link, and publication by a trusted GitHub Actions OIDC publisher. Browser binaries and Linux dependencies are downloaded during installation unless supplied by a pinned image/cache, so versions, lockfiles, image digests, egress, and Dependabot/security updates should be controlled. The browser process executes untrusted web content and should run with CI isolation; official Docker guidance distinguishes trusted E2E sites from untrusted scraping and recommends a non-root user/seccomp for the latter.
cost_and_risk.custom_harness_burden: Moderate and primarily application-specific. Playwright supplies browser, fixture, API, readiness, artifact, and teardown primitives. This repository still needs package/config files, an E2E workflow, Docker Compose startup/readiness, Flyway completion checks, deterministic PostgreSQL seed/reset and cleanup, Yahoo Finance replacement at the correct server/browser boundary, backend/service log attachment, and sensitive-artifact policy. Existing build/start/destroy scripts help but production start persists PostgreSQL data, so disposable CI volumes and explicit cleanup are necessary.
cost_and_risk.capability_delivery_tier: Core: TypeScript runner, browser management, locators, auto-waiting, assertions, isolation, API requests, network interception, projects, workers, retries, sharding, visual snapshots, traces, video, screenshots, downloads, reports, Inspector, UI Mode, and codegen. Official companion/integration: VS Code extension, Microsoft Docker images, and documented @axe-core/playwright use. Custom repository code: Compose/Flyway/PostgreSQL lifecycle, database disposal, backend log collection, Yahoo Finance backend mocking when server-side, artifact redaction policy, and long-term flake trends. Paid cloud: none required; hosted dashboards/grids are optional third-party capabilities.
cost_and_risk.ai_execution_boundary: The deterministic test runner, browser actions, assertions, retries, and CI do not require an LLM, network egress to an AI service, AI credentials, or per-run model cost. Codegen, locator picking, and ordinary debugging are local non-LLM features. Optional Playwright CLI/MCP or third-party AI authoring tools should remain outside required CI, receive least-privilege credentials and synthetic data, and produce reviewed TypeScript tests that continue to run without AI.
